errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to finish the sentence stating what the error is less than.
errors.name: Comparison with the tolerance left incomplete
non_conceptual_causes: assumption that the comparison is obvious
errors.observed_behavior: The response computes the bounding value but never states that it is at most the tolerance the prompt named.
errors.scoring_consequence: The communication point requires the inequality against the tolerance to be presented (sg-23:20, sg-22:21).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to name the two factors being differentiated before writing anything.
errors.name: Higher derivative computed without the product or chain rule
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99013.
errors.observed_behavior: The response differentiates a relation defining a derivative and omits a product rule factor or a chain rule factor.
errors.scoring_consequence: The form of the rule is scored separately from the resulting derivative, so an omitted factor loses the second point while the first may survive (sg-23:19).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the coefficient of the second degree term is when the second derivative at the centre is six.
errors.name: Taylor coefficient written without dividing by the factorial
errors.observed_behavior: The response places the derivative value directly as the coefficient of the power, with no factorial denominator.
errors.scoring_consequence: The polynomial is not the requested one and its term points are lost (sg-23:19).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what degree the requested polynomial has and which terms belong to it.
errors.name: Polynomial presented with extra terms or a trailing ellipsis
non_conceptual_causes: habit carried over from a series question
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes a polynomial that includes terms beyond the requested degree, or appends an ellipsis, turning the answer into a series.
errors.scoring_consequence: A polynomial with terms of higher degree, or with an ellipsis, does not earn the final polynomial point (sg-23:20, sg-23:21).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which derivative belongs in the coefficient of the third degree term and why.
errors.name: Derivative values taken from the wrong row or order
errors.observed_behavior: The response reads a table of derivative values and pairs a derivative of one order with the power of another.
errors.scoring_consequence: Each misplaced value spoils the term that depends on it.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which derivative appears in the bound for a fourth degree polynomial.
errors.name: Lagrange bound assembled in the wrong form
non_conceptual_causes: off by one slip in the order
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99016.
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the bound without the maximum of the next derivative, with the wrong power of the difference, or with the wrong factorial.
errors.scoring_consequence: The form point is lost, and with it the comparison point that depends on it (sg-23:20).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the series alternates and whether a bound on the next derivative is available.
errors.name: Error bound chosen whose conditions the situation does not meet
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99016.
errors.observed_behavior: The response reaches for the Lagrange bound where the alternating series bound is the available tool, or the reverse, without checking the conditions.
errors.scoring_consequence: A bound whose conditions are not met earns no justification point (sg-24:21).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the first two terms of the series at that endpoint.
errors.name: Endpoint value substituted into the wrong place in the general term
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99017.
errors.observed_behavior: The response substitutes the endpoint for the index rather than for the variable, or drops the alternating factor produced by a negative endpoint.
errors.scoring_consequence: The endpoint series is wrong, so the analysis and interval points are lost (sg-25:25).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the two inequalities that the absolute value statement stands for.
errors.name: Absolute value dropped when the ratio inequality is solved
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99037.
errors.observed_behavior: The response converts the inequality on the ratio into a one sided inequality, producing a half interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: An inequality in absolute value alone is not sufficient for the interior point; the compound inequality is required (sg-22:21, sg-25:25).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask how far the interval reaches from its centre.
errors.name: Interval presented where the radius of convergence was requested
errors.observed_behavior: The response solves the inequality and presents an interval without naming the radius as a value.
errors.scoring_consequence: The radius point cannot be earned by presenting an interval alone (sg-21:24).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the series becomes at each end of the interval.
errors.name: Endpoints of the interval left untested
non_conceptual_causes: time pressure at the end of the section
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99017.
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports the open interval found from the ratio test as the interval of convergence without examining either endpoint.
errors.scoring_consequence: Both the endpoint consideration point and the interval point are lost (sg-25:24).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which endpoints belong to the interval and how the notation shows that.
errors.name: Interval reported with endpoint inclusion that contradicts the endpoint analysis
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99037.
errors.observed_behavior: The response tests the endpoints correctly and then writes an interval whose brackets do not match the findings, or attaches a closed bracket to an unbounded end.
errors.scoring_consequence: The final interval point requires the interval to match the analysis (sg-25:25).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to substitute n equal to one and two into the proposed general term.
errors.name: General term of a series mis-differentiated or mis-assembled
non_conceptual_causes: off by one slip in the index
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99018.
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes several correct terms but produces a general term that does not reproduce them, often after differentiating with respect to the index or mishandling the alternating factor.
errors.scoring_consequence: The general term is a separate scored point from the first terms (sg-25:26, sg-24:22).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the first three terms of the series for the cosine and for the exponential separately.
errors.name: Standard Maclaurin series recalled incorrectly
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the series for the exponential, the sine, the cosine, or one over one minus x with wrong signs, wrong parities of the powers, or missing factorials.
errors.scoring_consequence: Every term built on the misremembered series is wrong, so the dependent points are lost (sg-23:21).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the second term becomes when the substitution is written with parentheses.
errors.name: Substitution into a known series carried out incorrectly
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99009.
errors.observed_behavior: The response substitutes an expression for the variable in a known series but does not raise the whole expression to the required power, or loses a constant factor.
errors.scoring_consequence: The resulting series is wrong from the first affected term onward.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the CED says about the radius of a term-by-term derivative.
errors.name: Radius of a differentiated or integrated series recomputed or claimed to change
non_conceptual_causes: algebra slip in the repeated ratio test
errors.observed_behavior: The response asserts a different radius for the derived series, or redoes the ratio test and reports a value inconsistent with the original radius.
errors.scoring_consequence: The radius point rests on the preservation statement, so an inconsistent value loses it (sg-24:22).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask where the input sits relative to the interval found earlier.
errors.name: Convergence at a specified input asserted without a reason
non_conceptual_causes: time pressure at the end of the question
assumption that the reason is obvious
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99001.
errors.observed_behavior: The response states that the series does or does not converge at the given input without placing the input relative to the interval of convergence.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer with reason point requires the position relative to the interval to be given (sg-25:27).

errors.discriminating_probe: Give the same function on an interval of length one and then on an interval of length four and ask for both averages.
errors.name: Average value reported without dividing by the interval length
errors.observed_behavior: The response presents the correct definite integral and reports its value as the average.
errors.scoring_consequence: The average value point is lost unless the correct answer appears elsewhere as evidence of the division (sg-25:3).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to underline the interval in the prompt before writing the quotient.
errors.name: Average taken over an interval the question did not name
errors.observed_behavior: The limits of the average value integral, or the divisor, come from an interval other than the one the prompt states.
errors.scoring_consequence: Both the setup point and the answer point are lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the integral of a rate that is negative on the whole interval.
errors.name: Region below the axis counted as positive area in an average
errors.observed_behavior: A graph dipping below the axis contributes a positive amount to the integral used in the average.
errors.scoring_consequence: The value is wrong, so the answer point is lost while the formula point may stand.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the student entered into the calculator, written as an integral.
errors.name: Calculator answer presented with no setup
non_conceptual_causes: a belief that the work is scratch
errors.observed_behavior: A decimal appears with no integral and no evidence of the division.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost; an unsupported value can still earn an answer point only where the guideline says so (sg-25:3).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the same computation with the unrounded stored value and compare.
errors.name: Intermediate value rounded before the final computation
errors.observed_behavior: A stored decimal is truncated to two or three places and then used in a later step, moving the reported answer.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost for inappropriate rounding, and at most one point per question is withheld on this ground (sg-25:2).

errors.discriminating_probe: Show both expressions side by side and ask for the units of each.
errors.name: Average value computed where an average rate of change was asked, or the reverse
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The response builds a difference quotient when the average of the function values was requested, or an integral quotient when the average rate of change was requested.
errors.scoring_consequence: Neither the setup point nor the answer point is earned, because the quantity is not the one asked for (sg-25:4).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the units of the integrand and of the differential separately and then multiply them.
errors.name: Units omitted or built from the wrong factors
errors.observed_behavior: A reported value carries no units, or units that are the rate units rather than the rate units multiplied by the input units.
errors.scoring_consequence: The units point, where one exists, is lost; in 2025 the units for an average rate of change were scored as their own point (sg-25:11).

errors.discriminating_probe: Give a velocity that is positive then negative and ask for both quantities in the same part.
errors.name: Displacement reported where total distance was asked
errors.observed_behavior: The response integrates velocity without the absolute value and reports the result as the distance travelled.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost because the integrand is wrong, and the answer point falls with it (sg-24:6).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the speed of a particle whose velocity is negative at that instant.
errors.name: Speed written without the absolute value or the magnitude
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The integrand for total distance is the velocity itself rather than its absolute value.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the value of the integral on each side of the zero of velocity before the total is requested.
errors.name: Interval not split where velocity changes sign
errors.observed_behavior: The response integrates velocity over the whole interval and takes one absolute value at the end.
errors.scoring_consequence: The value is too small, so the answer point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Give the same rate with two different starting amounts and ask for the later value in each case.
errors.name: Initial value not added to the accumulated change
errors.observed_behavior: The response evaluates the integral of the rate and reports it as the value of the quantity.
errors.scoring_consequence: The initial condition point is lost and the answer point falls with it (sg-24:7).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the number would be if the starting amount were doubled.
errors.name: Net change reported as the amount present
errors.observed_behavior: A question asking how much is present at a time is answered with the net change over the interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost even when the integral is correct.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the net rate should be at a time when the two rates are equal.
errors.name: Inflow and outflow rates added instead of subtracted
errors.observed_behavior: The net rate is written as the sum of the two rates, or the difference is taken in the wrong order.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to read the integrand aloud and say which terms the minus sign reaches.
errors.name: Parentheses lost when a supplied expression is placed in an integrand
errors.observed_behavior: A subtracted rate or a difference is substituted without parentheses, so only its first term is affected by the operation.
errors.scoring_consequence: The integrand is wrong, so the setup point is lost; the Chief Reader records this behaviour across questions.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the value at the endpoint has been compared with the value at the critical point.
errors.name: Local argument offered for an absolute extremum
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: A first or second derivative test is presented as the justification that an accumulated amount is largest.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost while the answer point remains available (sg-25:5).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the value of the amount at both ends of the interval.
errors.name: Endpoints omitted from a candidates table
errors.observed_behavior: The candidates test evaluates the amount only at the interior critical point.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost because the argument is not global (sg-25:5).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what would change in the sentence if the limits were different.
errors.name: Interpretation names the quantity but not the interval
errors.observed_behavior: The sentence says what is accumulating without saying between which inputs.
errors.scoring_consequence: The interpretation point is lost because the guideline requires the interval as well as the quantity (sg-23:2).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to name the variable of integration in the expression as written.
errors.name: Differential omitted from an integral expression
errors.observed_behavior: An integral is written with limits and an integrand but no dx, dt, or dy.
errors.scoring_consequence: Whether the point survives depends on the guideline; in 2023 a missing differential kept the setup point but could block the answer point when the expression was also equated to a value (sg-23:8).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which two inputs bound the region and why.
errors.name: Limits of integration taken from the wrong inputs
errors.observed_behavior: The integral is set up with limits that are not the boundary of the region or the interval requested.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost, and in 2023 incorrect limits also made a response ineligible for the final area point (sg-23:16).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to evaluate both functions at one interior input and say which is larger.
errors.name: Difference of the boundary functions taken in the wrong order
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The integrand is the lower curve minus the upper curve, or the left curve minus the right curve.
errors.scoring_consequence: The integrand point may survive, since either order earned it in 2023, but a negative value reported as an area loses the answer point (sg-23:16, sg-23:17).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to check the statement by evaluating both sides.
errors.name: Area asserted to equal an expression that is its negative
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the reversed difference, sets it equal to the positive area, and reports the positive value.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost for the incorrect statement even though the reported number is right (sg-23:17).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the lower limit becomes after the substitution and why.
errors.name: Limits kept in the old variable after a substitution
errors.observed_behavior: An antiderivative found by substitution is evaluated at the original limits without converting them.
errors.scoring_consequence: The response is not eligible for the answer point (sg-23:17).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to name the variable of integration and to check that the integrand contains only that variable.
errors.name: Integrand written in one variable with the differential of another
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: A function of x is integrated with respect to y, or the reverse, without being rewritten.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost because the expression does not define a number.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the smallest and largest y value in the region.
errors.name: Limits given as values of the variable not being integrated
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: An integral in y carries x values as its limits.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost and the value is wrong.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask how many solutions the equation of the two curves has on the interval.
errors.name: An interior intersection point not found
errors.observed_behavior: Only the outer two crossings are used, so an interior crossing is integrated across.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost because part of the region is subtracted rather than added.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the sign of the integrand on each side of the crossing.
errors.name: One integral used across a crossing of the curves
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: A fixed order of subtraction is integrated over an interval in which the curves exchange places.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reported area is smaller than the true area and the setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the integral would give if the two lobes had equal area.
errors.name: Absolute value dropped from a split region integrand
errors.observed_behavior: The single integral form is written without the absolute value bars around the difference.
errors.scoring_consequence: The value returned is the signed difference of the lobes, so the answer point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to mark the slice on the figure and label both of its ends.
errors.name: Cross sectional side written as one function value
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The side of the slice is taken as the upper curve alone although the region is bounded by two curves.
errors.scoring_consequence: The integrand is wrong, so the setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which shape the area formula in the integrand describes.
errors.name: Factor of pi placed in a polygonal cross section integrand
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: A square or triangular cross section volume carries a factor of pi.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost because the integrand belongs to the wrong volume family.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to expand both expressions for a specific pair of numbers and compare.
errors.name: Square of a difference used where a difference of squares is needed
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: A washer integrand is written as the square of the difference of the two radii, or a squared difference is expanded term by term.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost, and the value is wrong by the cross term.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the area of one slice with both dimensions labelled.
errors.name: Second dimension of a rectangular cross section omitted
errors.observed_behavior: A rectangular section whose height is a stated multiple of its base is treated as a square.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the area of a single slice of the named shape with a numerical side.
errors.name: Constant factor of a cross sectional area formula wrong or missing
errors.observed_behavior: The area of an equilateral or semicircular section is written without its fractional constant.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which side of the triangle lies in the base region.
errors.name: Distance between the curves used as a leg when it is the hypotenuse
errors.observed_behavior: A right isosceles section is given the leg formula although the stated distance is the hypotenuse.
errors.scoring_consequence: The integrand is off by a factor of two, so the setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the radius of a semicircle whose diameter is a stated length.
errors.name: Distance between the curves used as the radius of a semicircle
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The semicircular section is given a radius equal to the whole distance between the boundary curves.
errors.scoring_consequence: The volume is four times too large and the setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the area of a semicircle of a stated radius.
errors.name: Full circle area used for a semicircular cross section
errors.observed_behavior: The area formula omits the factor of one half that makes the section a semicircle.
errors.scoring_consequence: The volume is twice the correct value and the setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the area of one disc of a stated radius.
errors.name: Radius left unsquared in a solid of revolution integrand
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The disc integrand is pi times the function rather than pi times the square of the function.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the area of a circular slice of that radius is.
errors.name: Factor of pi omitted from a solid of revolution integrand
errors.observed_behavior: A disc or washer volume is reported without the constant factor pi.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the distance from a point on the curve to the stated line.
errors.name: Radius measured from a coordinate axis when the axis of revolution is elsewhere
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The response revolves about a line other than an axis but writes the radius as the bare function value.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which inputs the region occupies, independently of where the axis is.
errors.name: Limits of integration moved along with the axis of revolution
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The interval of integration is translated by the same amount as the axis.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost and the value is wrong.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which curve is farther from the axis at one interior input.
errors.name: Outer and inner radii of a washer exchanged
errors.observed_behavior: The nearer curve is used as the outer radius, giving a negative integrand.
errors.scoring_consequence: A negative volume is reported and the answer point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the length of a straight segment of slope one on an interval of length one should be.
errors.name: Arc length integrand written without the radical or without the added one
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The length integral is written as the integral of the derivative, or of the square root of the derivative squared alone.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the integrand for a linear function and compare with the Pythagorean length.
errors.name: Derivative not squared inside the arc length radical
errors.observed_behavior: The integrand is the square root of one plus the derivative.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the limits of the integral tell about the piece of curve being measured.
errors.name: Arc length identified without naming the interval
errors.observed_behavior: The response says the integral gives the length of the curve but does not say on which interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: The interval point is lost while the arc length point stands (sg-24:16).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the integrand would be if the area under the graph were wanted.
errors.name: Arc length integral described as an area
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The displayed radical integral is interpreted as the area under the graph.
errors.scoring_consequence: The identification point is lost (sg-24:16).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the expression that produced the number.
errors.name: Numerical length or volume reported with no integral shown
errors.observed_behavior: A decimal appears for an arc length or a volume with no integral expression anywhere in the response.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which conditions the theorem requires before the conclusion may be drawn.
errors.name: Theorem hypotheses not stated before the conclusion is used
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response applies the Mean Value Theorem or the Extreme Value Theorem and never mentions continuity or differentiability on the stated interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost even when the conclusion is correct, because the guideline makes the continuity statement a condition of that point.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask why the function is continuous on the closed interval.
errors.name: Continuity not drawn from the given differentiability
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response asserts that the function is continuous without saying that differentiability supplies it, or omits continuity altogether.
errors.scoring_consequence: The point tied to the hypothesis is lost; the 2025 guideline refused a bare statement that the function is continuous.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the units of the quantity just computed.
errors.name: Average rate of change formed incorrectly
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response averages the two endpoint values, reverses the order of subtraction, or divides by the wrong difference.
errors.scoring_consequence: The point for the average rate of change is lost and any solved value built on it is wrong.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to state the conclusion in one sentence.
errors.name: Existence asserted with no affirmative answer or no theorem
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response computes the needed arithmetic but never says yes and never names a theorem.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost; the guideline requires an affirmative answer in some form.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the reported input lies strictly between the endpoints.
errors.name: Solved value reported outside the open interval
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response solves the derivative equation and reports a solution that is an endpoint or lies outside the interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost because the theorem places the point strictly inside the interval.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which theorem concerns values of the function and which concerns values of the derivative.
errors.name: Intermediate Value Theorem cited for a claim about the derivative
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response justifies the existence of an input with a given derivative value by appealing to the Intermediate Value Theorem.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost outright; the 2023 guideline names this as disqualifying.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what would happen on the same interval for a function with a jump in the middle.
errors.name: Extreme Value Theorem invoked without continuity on the closed interval
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response claims that a maximum and a minimum are attained for a function with a break inside the interval, or on an open interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: The hypothesis point is lost and the conclusion is unsupported.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the theorem tells you and what it does not tell you.
errors.name: Existence theorem used to locate the extremum
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response treats the Extreme Value Theorem as though it named the input at which the extremum occurs.
errors.scoring_consequence: The response answers a different question and the location it reports is unsupported.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what equation produced the listed inputs.
errors.name: Zeros of the derivative listed without stating the derivative condition
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes down the inputs at which the derivative vanishes but never presents the equation setting the derivative equal to zero.
errors.scoring_consequence: The first point of the candidates test is lost; the 2023 guideline states that listing the zeros is not sufficient.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the function has a value at the disputed input.
errors.name: Solutions outside the domain retained as critical points
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response keeps an input at which the derivative expression vanishes although the function itself is undefined there.
errors.scoring_consequence: The candidate list is wrong and the comparison that follows cannot be correct.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to mark every input where the derivative graph breaks.
errors.name: Inputs where the derivative fails to exist omitted from the critical points
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response finds only the zeros of the derivative and skips corners, cusps, and vertical tangents.
errors.scoring_consequence: A candidate is missing, so the comparison may select the wrong extremum and the justification is incomplete.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether any other input could give a larger value.
errors.name: Relative extremum reported as the absolute extremum
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response finds a local high or low point and reports it as the largest or smallest value on the interval without comparing the rest.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost because the argument is local where a global claim was asked for.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the sign of the derivative is immediately on each side of the input.
errors.name: Critical point with no sign change declared an extremum
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports a relative maximum or minimum at an input where the derivative is zero but keeps its sign on both sides.
errors.scoring_consequence: The single answer with reason point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the value of the derivative at one input inside the disputed interval.
errors.name: Sign of the derivative misread on an interval
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response assigns the wrong sign to the derivative expression on one of the intervals of its sign chart.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reported intervals are wrong, which also forfeits the reason point.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to label the plotted curve and the function under discussion separately before answering.
errors.name: Plotted derivative read as the function itself
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response answers a question about the function by describing features of the curve shown, which is the derivative.
errors.scoring_consequence: Every part that rests on the plotted object is answered about the wrong function.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for a curve that is decreasing and concave up at the same time.
errors.name: Increase of the derivative confused with positivity of the derivative
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports concavity where monotonicity was asked for, or reports increase of the function where the derivative graph is rising.
errors.scoring_consequence: The intervals reported belong to the other question and the reason point is unavailable.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the domain of the function before the sign chart is drawn.
errors.name: Sign chart omits a point where the function is undefined
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response partitions the number line at the zeros of the derivative only and ignores a vertical asymptote or a domain gap.
errors.scoring_consequence: An interval spans a break, so the reported behaviour is claimed where the function does not exist.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to rewrite the sentence with every pronoun replaced by a name.
errors.name: Justification uses an unnamed referent
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The reason says that the function or the graph changes sign, without naming which object is meant.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reason point is lost; the 2025 guideline names an ambiguous referent as disqualifying.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the function has a value at the input between the two stretches.
errors.name: Interval of increase reported across a gap in the domain
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response merges two intervals of increase into one although the function is undefined between them.
errors.scoring_consequence: The interval reported is wrong and the reason point falls with it.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask where a relative extremum is allowed to occur.
errors.name: Candidate extrema sought away from the critical points
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response tests inputs that are neither critical points nor endpoints when hunting for a relative extremum.
errors.scoring_consequence: Time is spent on inputs that cannot be extrema, and in a candidates argument extra inputs cost the justification point.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to sketch the curve implied by their own sign statement.
errors.name: Direction of the sign change reversed in the classification
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports a relative maximum where the derivative changes from negative to positive, or the reverse.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer with reason point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the sign of the derivative is on each side, not its size.
errors.name: Classification taken from the value of the derivative rather than its change
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response classifies the critical point by whether the derivative is large or small nearby instead of by its sign change.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reason does not express a sign change, so the point is lost even when the classification is right.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to state whether the derivative changes sign, in those words.
errors.name: Positive before and after offered in place of no sign change
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response justifies a classification of neither by saying the derivative is positive before and after the input.
errors.scoring_consequence: The point is lost; the 2023 guideline names this phrasing as insufficient while accepting a declaration that the derivative does not change sign.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to read the question aloud and underline the noun that is asked for.
errors.name: Location reported where the value was asked for
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response names the input at which the extremum occurs when the question asked for the extreme value, or the reverse.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost; the 2023 guideline awarded it only for the minimum value, not for the input.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which of the listed inputs lie inside the stated interval.
errors.name: Critical points outside the interval included as candidates
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response carries a critical point that lies outside the closed interval into the candidate comparison.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost because inputs other than the candidates appear in the argument.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the function value is at each end of the interval.
errors.name: One or both endpoints omitted from the candidate comparison
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response compares values only at the interior critical points and never evaluates at the ends of the interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost; the 2023 guideline states that a response not considering both endpoints does not earn it.

errors.discriminating_probe: Recompute one disputed entry and compare with the table.
errors.name: Function evaluated incorrectly at a candidate
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: One entry of the candidate table is wrong, whether by substitution or by an area computation.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost outright; the 2023 guideline withholds it for any evaluation error at a candidate.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which of the tabulated values is smallest.
errors.name: Extremum selected in the wrong direction
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response compares the candidate values correctly but reports the largest where the smallest was asked for.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost although the table is right.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask how the candidate compares with the value at the far end of the interval.
errors.name: Local argument offered where a global argument is required
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response justifies an absolute extremum with a first derivative test or a second derivative test at the candidate.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost while the answer point stays available with the correct value.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the value of the second derivative at one input inside the disputed interval.
errors.name: Sign of the second derivative misread
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response assigns the wrong sign to the second derivative on one interval of its sign chart.
errors.scoring_consequence: The concavity intervals are wrong and the reason point is unavailable.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the plotted curve is rising or falling on the disputed stretch.
errors.name: Concavity read from the sign of the plotted derivative
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports concave up where the plotted derivative is above the axis rather than where it is rising.
errors.scoring_consequence: The intervals reported are those of increase, so both the interval point and the reason point are lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the function has a value at the disputed input.
errors.name: Second derivative zeros taken outside the domain of the function
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response lists a candidate point of inflection at an input where the function is not defined.
errors.scoring_consequence: The declared list contains an extra input, which costs the answer point.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the second derivative does on each side of the disputed input.
errors.name: Point of inflection declared with no sign change checked
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports every zero of the second derivative, or every zero of the plotted curve, as a point of inflection.
errors.scoring_consequence: An extra input in the list costs the answer point outright.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to sketch the second derivative near that input.
errors.name: Touching zero retained as a point of inflection
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response keeps an input where the second derivative reaches zero and returns to the same sign.
errors.scoring_consequence: The list has an extra entry, so the answer point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which plotted feature makes the second derivative change sign there.
errors.name: Inflection reason restated in second derivative symbols
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The reason says that the second derivative changes sign there, without tying the claim to the plotted object the question supplied.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reason point is lost while the answer point stands; the 2025 guideline names this split directly.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the value of the first derivative at that input.
errors.name: Second derivative test applied where the first derivative is not zero
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response evaluates the second derivative at an input that is not a critical point and classifies it.
errors.scoring_consequence: The conclusion does not follow and the justification point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to sketch a curve that is concave down at a critical point.
errors.name: Sign convention of the second derivative test reversed
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports a relative minimum where the second derivative is negative, or the reverse.
errors.scoring_consequence: The classification is wrong and the point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the first derivative does on each side of the input.
errors.name: Inconclusive case treated as a conclusion
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports neither a maximum nor a minimum because the second derivative is zero at the critical point.
errors.scoring_consequence: The classification is unsupported, since the test settles nothing in that case.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask how many critical points the function has on the interval.
errors.name: Sole critical point claim made without stating uniqueness
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response extends a relative extremum to an absolute one without saying that there is only one critical point on the interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification is incomplete because the step that makes the local claim global is missing.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which derivative the given object actually shows.
errors.name: Derivative test chosen that the given information cannot support
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response reaches for a second derivative test when only a graph of the first derivative is given and its slope is never discussed.
errors.scoring_consequence: The argument cannot be completed from the given information, so the justification point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask where the original curve has a horizontal tangent.
errors.name: Derivative sketch drawn with turning points at the zeros of the function
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response places the extrema of the derivative sketch where the original curve crosses the axis.
errors.scoring_consequence: The sketch fails every feature check that follows.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the derivative is at a point where the function has a relative maximum.
errors.name: Curve sketched with turning points at the zeros of the wrong object
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response draws the function with extrema where the derivative graph turns rather than where it crosses the axis.
errors.scoring_consequence: Extrema and points of inflection are interchanged throughout the sketch.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which derivative has to change sign for an extremum and which for a point of inflection.
errors.name: Feature of the function matched with the wrong derivative
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response pairs a point of inflection with a zero of the first derivative, or an extremum with a zero of the second.
errors.scoring_consequence: Every answer that rests on the correspondence is displaced by one derivative.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask where the derivative graph reaches its own extreme value.
errors.name: Point of inflection drawn at a turning point of the sketch
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The sketch puts a change of bending exactly where the curve has a horizontal tangent with no justification.
errors.scoring_consequence: The sketch contradicts the derivative information it was built from.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether shifting the sketch up by one unit would still fit the derivative.
errors.name: Sketch treated as unique with no reference to the constant
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response asserts that one particular curve is the graph of the function when only the derivative was supplied.
errors.scoring_consequence: The claim is stronger than the information supports unless a value of the function was given.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which curve has zeros at the turning points of which other curve.
errors.name: Three graphs ordered in the reverse derivative direction
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response labels the function as the second derivative and the second derivative as the function.
errors.scoring_consequence: Every feature question about the triple is answered about the wrong object.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the sign, not the direction, of the second derivative on that stretch.
errors.name: Concavity read from the wrong direction of the second derivative
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response states that the graph is concave up where the second derivative is decreasing rather than positive.
errors.scoring_consequence: The concavity claim is wrong and any inflection list built from it inherits the error.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which expression has to change sign for the behaviour in question.
errors.name: Sign table built on the zeros of the function
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response partitions the number line at the zeros of the function instead of at the zeros of its derivatives.
errors.scoring_consequence: The partition does not align with the sign changes that matter, so the reported behaviour is wrong.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether another function through the same table could behave differently between the listed inputs.
errors.name: Finite table read as settling behaviour between the listed inputs
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response claims monotonicity or concavity across a whole interval from three tabulated derivative values.
errors.scoring_consequence: The claim exceeds what the data support and cannot earn a justification point.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what each letter stands for and in what units.
errors.name: Variables used without being defined
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes an objective and a constraint in letters that are never given meanings or units.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is at risk and the interpretation that follows has nothing to name.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask how many unknowns remain in the expression about to be differentiated.
errors.name: Constraint not substituted, leaving two variables
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response differentiates an expression that still contains both unknowns.
errors.scoring_consequence: The derivative is not the derivative of a one variable objective, so the critical point is wrong.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which values of the variable the situation permits.
errors.name: Contextual domain omitted or taken as all inputs
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response never states the range of inputs the situation allows and treats the objective as defined everywhere.
errors.scoring_consequence: Endpoints that could hold the extremum are never considered and the verification is incomplete.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which variable the reduced objective is a function of.
errors.name: Objective differentiated with respect to the wrong variable
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response differentiates with respect to a variable that the constraint has already eliminated.
errors.scoring_consequence: The derivative is meaningless for the reduced objective and the critical point is wrong.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask how the student knows the critical point is not the opposite kind of extremum.
errors.name: No verification that the critical point gives the extremum
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response stops once the derivative is zero and reports the value as the maximum or minimum.
errors.scoring_consequence: The verification point is lost, and the reported extremum is unsupported on the stated domain.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the number counts or measures.
errors.name: Units omitted from the reported optimum
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response gives a number for the optimal value and never names its units.
errors.scoring_consequence: An interpretation point that requires units is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what would change in the sentence if the interval were different.
errors.name: Interpretation omits the quantity or the input where the extremum occurs
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The interpretation sentence names a number without saying what it measures or when it is attained.
errors.scoring_consequence: The interpretation point is lost because the sentence is incomplete.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the value of the denominator at the reported point.
errors.name: Horizontal tangent points found without checking the denominator
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response sets the numerator of the derivative to zero and reports points where the denominator also vanishes.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reported points may have no tangent at all, so the critical point list is wrong.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the reported coordinates satisfy the defining equation.
errors.name: Vertical tangent points reported without a matching point on the relation
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response solves the denominator equal to zero and reports the solutions without checking they lie on the curve.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reported points are not on the relation, so the answer is unsupported.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which points of the curve have that input value.
errors.name: One coordinate reported where a point was asked for
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response gives an input value alone as the location of a horizontal tangent on a relation.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer is incomplete because a relation may pass through several outputs at that input.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the derivative of the square of the dependent variable with respect to the independent one is.
errors.name: Second derivative of a relation taken as though the second variable were constant
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response differentiates the derivative expression without applying the chain rule to the dependent variable.
errors.scoring_consequence: The differentiation point is lost, and the value point remains available only through a correct substitution.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the value of the first derivative at the given point, then reread the expression.
errors.name: First derivative left unsubstituted in the second derivative
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports a second derivative expression that still contains the derivative symbol when a number was asked for.
errors.scoring_consequence: The substitution point is lost; the 2025 guideline treats the differentiation and the substitution as separate points.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which way the curve bends when the second derivative is negative.
errors.name: Sign of the second derivative at the point misread for the classification
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response evaluates the second derivative on a relation correctly but classifies the point the wrong way round.
errors.scoring_consequence: The classification is wrong although the computation was right.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the units of the number just written.
errors.name: Difference reported without the quotient
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports the change in the function values over the interval without dividing by the change in the inputs.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point requires both a difference and a quotient using values from the table, so a difference alone does not earn it (sg-25:11).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the value of the expression just written.
errors.name: Quotient expression presented with no evaluated value
non_conceptual_causes: treating the setup as the answer
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the difference quotient correctly but stops before producing a number.
errors.scoring_consequence: The quotient presented by itself is not sufficient for the answer point (sg-25:11).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the denominator of the quotient measures.
errors.name: Units omitted or given as the units of the quantity
non_conceptual_causes: copying units from the table header
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports an estimated derivative with no units, or with the units of the modelled quantity rather than of its rate.
errors.scoring_consequence: The units point is lost; it is earned for the correct compound units whether or not they are attached to a value, and an equivalent compound form is accepted (sg-25:11).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which interval the question names and which rows carry its endpoints.
errors.name: Rows used that do not match the requested interval
errors.observed_behavior: The response estimates the derivative from a pair of tabulated inputs other than the pair the question names or the pair that brackets the point.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost because the supporting work does not use the values the question specifies.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the denominator is at the moment the substitution is made.
errors.name: Increment set to zero before the common factor is divided out
errors.observed_behavior: The response substitutes zero for the increment while it is still in the denominator.
errors.scoring_consequence: The simplification point and the value point are both lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to read aloud what the second line of the work asserts.
errors.name: Limit symbol dropped during the computation
non_conceptual_causes: notational shorthand carried over from class
errors.observed_behavior: The response manipulates the difference quotient without carrying the limit symbol and attaches it only to the final line.
errors.scoring_consequence: A notation point is lost where the definition itself is being assessed.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to evaluate the function at a specific numerical shifted input and compare with the expansion.
errors.name: Shifted term expanded incorrectly
errors.observed_behavior: The response expands the function evaluated at the shifted input as though the function distributed over the sum.
errors.scoring_consequence: The simplification point and the value point are both lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to point to the limit in the work.
errors.name: Derivative produced by rule where the definition was demanded
errors.observed_behavior: The response differentiates with the power rule and presents the result as an application of the definition.
errors.scoring_consequence: The points attached to the difference quotient and its simplification are lost although the final value may be right.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to name a function whose values appear in the numerator.
errors.name: Limit in derivative form reported as nonexistent
non_conceptual_causes: not testing the difference quotient shape
errors.observed_behavior: The response treats a limit having the shape of a difference quotient as indeterminate and unresolvable.
errors.scoring_consequence: The value point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which value of the function is subtracted in the numerator.
errors.name: Wrong base point identified in a limit read as a derivative
errors.observed_behavior: The response identifies the underlying function correctly but evaluates its derivative at the wrong input.
errors.scoring_consequence: The value point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what in the question tells the student that the function is continuous.
errors.name: Continuity asserted with no basis in an argument about a differentiable function
errors.observed_behavior: The response states that the function is continuous without saying that it is continuous because it is differentiable.
errors.scoring_consequence: The continuity point requires the reason; a bare statement that the function is continuous does not earn it (sg-25:12).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for a function continuous at a point at which it has no derivative.
errors.name: Implication run backwards from continuity to differentiability
non_conceptual_causes: symmetry assumed between the two properties
errors.observed_behavior: The response concludes that a function is differentiable at a point because it is continuous there.
errors.scoring_consequence: A justification point is lost because the claim is not supported by the theorem.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the slope approached from the left and from the right as two separate values.
errors.name: Non-differentiability claimed from the appearance of the graph alone
errors.observed_behavior: The response says the derivative does not exist because the graph looks sharp, without reference to the one sided slopes.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reason point is lost although the verdict may be correct.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the slope of a vertical line is.
errors.name: Vertical tangent treated as a horizontal one
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports the derivative at a vertical tangent as zero.
errors.scoring_consequence: The verdict point is lost because a value is reported where none exists.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to differentiate a squared term from the definition and compare with the rule.
errors.name: Exponent reduced without multiplying by it
errors.observed_behavior: The response lowers the exponent by one but omits the factor of the original exponent.
errors.scoring_consequence: The derivative point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the graph of a constant function looks like and what its slope is.
errors.name: Constant term differentiated to itself
errors.observed_behavior: The response carries a constant term unchanged into the derivative.
errors.scoring_consequence: The derivative point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the term as a power of the variable first.
errors.name: Radical or reciprocal left undifferentiated
errors.observed_behavior: The response differentiates the polynomial terms and copies a radical or reciprocal term unchanged.
errors.scoring_consequence: The derivative point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the slope of the cosine graph just to the right of zero.
errors.name: Sign dropped from the derivative of cosine
errors.observed_behavior: The response gives sine as the derivative of cosine without the negative sign.
errors.scoring_consequence: The derivative point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which of the base and the exponent is the variable.
errors.name: Exponential differentiated by the power rule
non_conceptual_causes: pattern matching on the shape of the expression
errors.observed_behavior: The response treats the natural exponential as a power of the variable and reduces its exponent.
errors.scoring_consequence: The derivative point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to expand a simple product, differentiate it term by term, and compare with the proposed answer.
errors.name: Product differentiated as a product of derivatives
non_conceptual_causes: pattern matching on the sum rule
errors.observed_behavior: The response multiplies the derivatives of the two factors together.
errors.scoring_consequence: The rule point and the result point are both lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to apply the rule to a quotient whose derivative is already known and compare.
errors.name: Quotient rule numerator terms reversed
errors.observed_behavior: The response subtracts in the opposite order in the numerator of the quotient rule.
errors.scoring_consequence: The result point is lost because the derivative carries the wrong sign.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the derivative of a reciprocal by the quotient rule and compare with the power rule result.
errors.name: Denominator square omitted
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the quotient rule with the denominator rather than its square below the line.
errors.scoring_consequence: The result point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the denominator changes when the variable changes.
errors.name: Quotient rule applied where the denominator is constant
non_conceptual_causes: pattern matching on the shape of the expression
errors.observed_behavior: The response applies the full quotient rule to an expression whose denominator carries no variable.
errors.scoring_consequence: No point is necessarily lost but the additional algebra invites a further error.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to label each of the four supplied numbers before substituting.
errors.name: Function value used where a derivative value was required
errors.observed_behavior: The response substitutes the value of a function into a position in the product or quotient rule that calls for the value of its derivative.
errors.scoring_consequence: The value point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to derive the cofunction derivative from the quotient rule rather than from memory.
errors.name: Cofunction derivative given without its negative sign
errors.observed_behavior: The response gives the derivative of cotangent or cosecant without the negative sign.
errors.scoring_consequence: The result point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which rule applies to a quotient of two functions.
errors.name: Trigonometric quotient differentiated term by term
non_conceptual_causes: pattern matching on the sum rule
errors.observed_behavior: The response differentiates the numerator and the denominator of a rewritten trigonometric quotient separately.
errors.scoring_consequence: The rule point and the result point are both lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which of the two computed numbers is a slope and which is a height.
errors.name: Function value used as the slope of the tangent line
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the tangent line using the value of the function at the point as its slope.
errors.scoring_consequence: The slope point and the equation point are both lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask at which input the line touches the curve.
errors.name: Derivative evaluated at the wrong input for a tangent line
errors.observed_behavior: The response differentiates correctly but substitutes an input other than the point of tangency.
errors.scoring_consequence: The slope point is lost and the equation point with it.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the numerator of the Leibniz expression denotes on its own.
errors.name: Leibniz notation read as a quotient of two separate quantities
errors.observed_behavior: The response treats the Leibniz form as a fraction whose parts can be separated and cancelled.
errors.scoring_consequence: A notation point is lost where the meaning of the symbol is being assessed.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the requested object depends on the variable.
errors.name: Derivative function confused with its value at a point
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports a function where a number is requested, or a number where the function is requested.
errors.scoring_consequence: The conversion point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the expression the calculator was asked to evaluate.
errors.name: Calculator derivative reported without a setup
non_conceptual_causes: treating the calculator output as the work
errors.observed_behavior: The response gives a numerical derivative value with no indication of what was computed.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost although the value may be right.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the unrounded value the calculator displayed.
errors.name: Calculator value rounded to too few places
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports a decimal approximation to fewer than three places after the decimal point.
errors.scoring_consequence: An inappropriately rounded answer does not earn its point unless an earlier point in the same question was already lost to rounding (sg-25:4).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the units alone, with no computation, and compare them with the units in the stem.
errors.name: Units omitted or assembled the wrong way round
non_conceptual_causes: time pressure at the end of a part
the units are written on scratch work and not transferred
errors.observed_behavior: A correct numerical rate is reported with no units, or with the units of the quantity alone, or with the numerator and denominator units exchanged.
errors.scoring_consequence: The units point is a separate point in the 2024 and 2025 table based questions and is lost outright (sg-24:2, sg-25:11); BC-ERR-99005 records the same behaviour across years.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what would change in the sentence if the interval were different.
errors.name: Interpretation left incomplete
non_conceptual_causes: the sentence is abbreviated after a long computation
errors.observed_behavior: The interpretation names the quantity but omits the instant or interval, the direction of change, or the units.
errors.scoring_consequence: The interpretation point is lost; BC-ERR-99027 records incomplete interpretation in context across the Chief Reader reports.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which of the two quantities the units in the stem describe.
errors.name: Amount reported where a rate was requested
errors.observed_behavior: The response supplies a value of the modelled function where the question asked for a value of its derivative, or the reverse.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost; BC-ERR-99030 records confusion of the direction of change with the quantity itself.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which two table entries were used and what was done with them.
errors.name: Difference quotient presented without the difference
errors.observed_behavior: The approximation is written as a single quotient or as a bare number with no visible difference of tabulated values.
errors.scoring_consequence: The 2025 rubric states that the setup expression by itself is not sufficient for the point, which requires the answer together with a difference and a quotient using values from the table (sg-25:11).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the quantity was larger or smaller a moment later.
errors.name: Sign of a rate not interpreted
non_conceptual_causes: the minus sign is dropped in transcription
errors.observed_behavior: A negative rate is reported as a magnitude or is described as an increase.
errors.scoring_consequence: The interpretation point is lost; BC-ERR-99030 records the same confusion of direction with quantity.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write which function the stem supplied before differentiating.
errors.name: Differentiation performed the wrong number of times for the quantity requested
errors.observed_behavior: Acceleration is reported where velocity was asked for, or position where velocity was asked for.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost although each differentiation performed is correct.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether a speed can be negative and what the sign of the velocity records instead.
errors.name: Speed reported as a signed quantity
non_conceptual_causes: the absolute value is applied on scratch work and not transferred
errors.observed_behavior: A negative number is reported as the speed of the particle.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what quantity has to be negative for the particle to be moving in the negative direction.
errors.name: Direction of motion read from the position rather than the velocity
non_conceptual_causes: misread of which function is graphed
errors.observed_behavior: The response argues the direction of travel from whether the position is positive or negative.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reasoning point is lost; the 2022 Chief Reader report records responses arguing from the wrong function in a related part (cr-22:20).

errors.discriminating_probe: Give a case with negative velocity and positive acceleration and ask whether the particle is speeding up.
errors.name: Speed decided from the sign of the acceleration alone
non_conceptual_causes: the rule is recalled in an abbreviated form
errors.observed_behavior: The response concludes that the speed is increasing because the acceleration is positive, without considering the sign of the velocity.
errors.scoring_consequence: The speed point is lost; the 2022 report names this the most common misconception on that question and the 2025 report records responses addressing only the sign of the derivative of velocity (cr-22:21, crabbc-25:22). BC-ERR-99003 records the same behaviour across years.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to solve the equation velocity equal to zero explicitly.
errors.name: Zeros of velocity found by sampling integer times
non_conceptual_causes: the formula looks awkward to solve
errors.observed_behavior: Integer times are substituted into the velocity in place of solving the equation velocity equal to zero, so a non-integer zero is missed.
errors.scoring_consequence: The 2025 Chief Reader report records this behaviour directly and links it to the loss of the two analysis points, whose mean scores were 0.04 and 0.03 (crabbc-25:20, crabbc-25:22).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to state in one sentence what the chart says about the interval named in the prompt.
errors.name: Sign chart presented with no stated reading
non_conceptual_causes: the conclusion is judged obvious from the chart
errors.observed_behavior: A number line or table of signs appears with no sentence saying what it shows about the direction of motion over the interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: The 2025 report records that responses failing to communicate what the chart showed over the whole interval did not earn the analysis points (crabbc-25:22, crabbc-25:23); BC-ERR-99001 records vague referents in justification across years.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the letters in the model stand for before any computation is done.
errors.name: Quantity and independent variable not named
non_conceptual_causes: the naming is treated as unnecessary
errors.observed_behavior: The response computes without saying which quantity is modelled or what the input variable measures.
errors.scoring_consequence: Later interpretation points become unavailable because the answer cannot be tied to the situation; BC-ERR-99033 records variables introduced without being defined.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to name the quantity whose rate is being described.
errors.name: Motion vocabulary used for a non-motion quantity
non_conceptual_causes: habit carried over from the motion topic
errors.observed_behavior: The response calls the rate of change of a temperature, a population, or an area a velocity.
errors.scoring_consequence: The 2025 scoring notes show a response calling an average value an average velocity treated as unclear communication and scored as scratch work, so the points survived in that instance (sg-25:3); the CED nonetheless directs that context vocabulary be used (ced:84).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the limit expression before any evaluation.
errors.name: Arithmetic performed with infinity in place of a limit
errors.observed_behavior: An expression with infinity substituted into it is written and set equal to a value, rather than a limit expression being evaluated.
errors.scoring_consequence: The 2025 scoring notes state that arithmetic with infinity is treated as scratch work and does not earn the value point (sg-25:4); BC-ERR-99007 records the same behaviour across years.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write each rate in derivative notation and to mark which one is unknown.
errors.name: Given and requested rates not distinguished
errors.observed_behavior: The rate supplied in the stem is reported as the answer, or the requested rate is treated as known.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost; BC-ERR-99033 records variables introduced without being defined as a related communication failure.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to draw the configuration and label every length before writing a formula.
errors.name: Relating equation wrong or absent
errors.observed_behavior: No equation ties the quantities together, or the formula used does not describe the configuration.
errors.scoring_consequence: Nothing downstream can be earned; BC-ERR-99011 records integrands chosen from the wrong area or volume family as the analogous failure in Unit 8.
