errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what variable the requested rate is taken with respect to, before differentiating.
errors.name: Differentiation carried out with respect to the wrong variable
non_conceptual_causes: habit carried from the implicit differentiation topic
errors.observed_behavior: The relating equation is differentiated with respect to a length or with respect to x, and the response stops there rather than continuing through the chain rule to a rate with respect to time.
errors.scoring_consequence: The Chief Reader report for 2024 records that responses differentiating with respect to x needed to continue through the chain rule and that many provided no work beyond that step (cr-24:18); BC-ERR-99013 records the same family across years.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to name the two factors of the term before differentiating it.
errors.name: Product rule omitted inside a differentiation with respect to time
non_conceptual_causes: the term is short and is read as one symbol
errors.observed_behavior: A term that multiplies two varying quantities is differentiated as though one of them were constant.
errors.scoring_consequence: The completely correct differentiation point is lost; BC-ERR-99013 names the missing product rule explicitly.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask how many unknown rates the differentiated equation contains.
errors.name: Extra varying quantity never eliminated
non_conceptual_causes: the proportion is seen but not used
errors.observed_behavior: The relating equation keeps two varying dimensions that the supplied rates cannot support, and the differentiation produces an equation with two unknown rates.
errors.scoring_consequence: The requested rate cannot be isolated, so the answer point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which of the stated numbers would still be true one second later.
errors.name: Instantaneous values substituted before differentiating
non_conceptual_causes: the substitution is made to simplify the algebra
errors.observed_behavior: A dimension that varies with time is replaced by its value at the instant before the equation is differentiated, so its rate never appears.
errors.scoring_consequence: The differentiated equation is wrong and the answer follows it; the CED sample activity asks students to mark which given information always applies and which applies only at an instant, which is the distinction at stake (ced:86).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to name the single unknown in the equation and to isolate it.
errors.name: Requested rate never isolated
non_conceptual_causes: the algebra is left for later and not returned to
errors.observed_behavior: The differentiated equation is correct and the response stops without solving for the unknown rate.
errors.scoring_consequence: The final scoring point is lost although the differentiation points may be earned (cr-24:18).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which quantities the differentiated equation needs and which of them the stem supplies.
errors.name: Missing instantaneous value not computed
errors.observed_behavior: A quantity needed for the substitution is absent from the stem and the response substitutes nothing in its place or invents a value.
errors.scoring_consequence: The substitution is incomplete and the answer point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to check that the point satisfies the line they wrote.
errors.name: Tangent line written with the point and the slope exchanged
errors.observed_behavior: The point-slope form is assembled incorrectly, so the coordinates appear where the slope belongs or the line does not pass through the point.
errors.scoring_consequence: The approximation point is lost; the 2025 report records multiple sign and parenthesis errors arising while isolating the dependent variable, which was not required (crabbc-25:25).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which input the question asks about and which one the tangent line was built at.
errors.name: Tangent line evaluated at the point of tangency
non_conceptual_causes: misread of which input is wanted
errors.observed_behavior: The approximation is produced by substituting the point of tangency rather than the nearby input, so the function value at the known point is returned.
errors.scoring_consequence: The approximation point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Give an increasing concave down function and ask for the direction of the tangent line error.
errors.name: Over or under estimate claimed without appealing to concavity
non_conceptual_causes: the claim is guessed when time runs short
confusion of the two derivative signs under pressure
errors.observed_behavior: The direction of the approximation error is asserted, or is argued from whether the function is increasing or decreasing rather than from how it bends.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost; BC-ERR-99020 records this behaviour across the Chief Reader reports (cr-22:18, cr-23:11).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what feature of the supplied representation makes the concavity claim true.
errors.name: Concavity asserted without reference to the given representation
non_conceptual_causes: the connection is made mentally and not written
errors.observed_behavior: The response states that the second derivative has a sign without connecting that claim to the graph, table, or formula supplied.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost; BC-ERR-99001 records vague referents in justifications and the 2023 report records reasons not connected to the given graph (cr-23:15).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which point the tangent line touches before the substitution is made.
errors.name: Supplied derivative evaluated at the wrong point
errors.observed_behavior: An expression for the derivative involving both coordinates is evaluated at coordinates other than the point of tangency.
errors.scoring_consequence: The slope point is lost, though the approximation point may still be earned on the incorrect slope (crabbc-25:25).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the numerator limit and the denominator limit as two separate statements.
errors.name: Quotient written explicitly equal to an indeterminate form
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the limit of the quotient equal to zero over zero rather than presenting the two limits separately.
errors.scoring_consequence: The 2023 rubric states that a response presenting a limit explicitly equal to zero over zero does not earn the first point, and the Chief Reader report names this arithmetic with infinity (sg-23:14, cr-23:15).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what would have to be true for the rule to be usable here.
errors.name: Rule applied with no verification of the form
errors.observed_behavior: The derivatives of numerator and denominator are taken with no statement that the limit was indeterminate.
errors.scoring_consequence: The hypothesis point is lost; the CED unit overview states that students must show that the rule applies, and BC-ERR-99008 records unverified hypotheses across years (ced:84).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the two derivatives on separate lines before forming the quotient.
errors.name: Quotient rule applied in place of separate derivatives
non_conceptual_causes: confusion of two rules under time pressure
errors.observed_behavior: The derivative of the whole quotient is taken rather than the quotient of the two derivatives.
errors.scoring_consequence: The application point is lost; the CED unit overview emphasises that the conclusion features the ratio of the derivatives rather than the derivative of the ratio (ced:84).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the derivative of each piece of the numerator separately.
errors.name: Derivative of an unknown function in the numerator taken incorrectly
non_conceptual_causes: the supplied value of the derivative is misread
errors.observed_behavior: The numerator contains a function known only through supplied properties and its derivative is mishandled, so the resulting limit is wrong.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost although the hypothesis and application points may be earned; the 2023 report records incorrect derivatives of the numerator or denominator as the common failure after a correct application (cr-23:15).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for each component derivative on its own before any quotient is formed.
errors.name: Component derivative computed incorrectly
errors.observed_behavior: One of dx/dt or dy/dt is wrong, so every later quantity built from it is wrong.
errors.scoring_consequence: The point that depends on that component is lost, though a declared incorrect component may be imported into later parts without further loss (sg-23:7).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the slope should be when the path is a straight line of slope two.
errors.name: Slope written as dx/dt divided by dy/dt
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The quotient of parametric derivatives is taken in the reciprocal order.
errors.scoring_consequence: The slope point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the units, or for the value of dx/dt, and see whether the division follows.
errors.name: Rate of the vertical component reported as the slope
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The response gives dy/dt where the slope of the tangent line was requested.
errors.scoring_consequence: The slope point is lost because the quotient structure is absent (sg-23:7).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the expression that the calculator evaluated.
errors.name: Slope value presented without the quotient
errors.observed_behavior: A correct decimal appears for the slope with no expression showing dy/dt divided by dx/dt.
errors.scoring_consequence: The point is not earned, because the guideline requires the communication of the quotient (sg-23:7).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what happens to the tangent line at a parameter value where dx/dt is zero.
errors.name: Condition that dx/dt is not zero omitted
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The slope formula is applied at a parameter value where dx/dt vanishes, or the condition is never mentioned where the question asks for it.
errors.scoring_consequence: A justification point that requires the hypothesis is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Recompute with the stored value and compare the third decimal place.
errors.name: Intermediate value rounded before a later step
errors.observed_behavior: A stored derivative, angle, or speed is truncated and then reused, moving the final answer.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost for inappropriate rounding, and at most one point per question is withheld on that ground (sg-25:6).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the coordinates of the particle at that time before the line is written.
errors.name: Tangent line written through the velocity components rather than the position
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The point used in the tangent line is the pair of derivative values instead of the coordinates of the particle.
errors.scoring_consequence: The tangent line is wrong even when the slope is right.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the slope is when dy/dt is zero and dx/dt is not.
errors.name: Horizontal and vertical tangent conditions exchanged
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The response solves dx/dt equal to zero for horizontal tangents.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reported parameter values are wrong.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to compute both expressions for a curve whose second derivative can be checked directly.
errors.name: Second derivative taken as a quotient of second derivatives
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The second derivative of y with respect to x is written as the second derivative of y with respect to t divided by the second derivative of x with respect to t.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which variable the second derivative is taken with respect to.
errors.name: Second division by dx/dt omitted
errors.observed_behavior: The derivative of dy/dx with respect to the parameter is reported as the second derivative of y with respect to x.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the expression that produced the number.
errors.name: Numerical answer presented with no setup
errors.observed_behavior: A decimal appears for a vector component, a length, an area, or a derivative with no supporting expression.
errors.scoring_consequence: An unsupported correct acceleration vector earned one of two points in 2023, and an unsupported distance earned neither of two (sg-23:6, sg-23:8).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which quantity has to be positive for the curve in the plane to bend upward.
errors.name: Concavity read from the sign of a component derivative
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The response decides whether the curve is concave up from the sign of the second derivative of y with respect to the parameter.
errors.scoring_consequence: The conclusion is unsupported and the justification point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the speed of a particle whose two component rates are three and four.
errors.name: Component rates added instead of combined as a magnitude
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The speed or the arc length integrand is the sum of the two rates rather than the square root of the sum of their squares.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to read the integrand aloud and say what the exponent reaches.
errors.name: Parentheses lost inside a squared component
errors.observed_behavior: A squared component is written so that only part of it is squared.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost while the answer point remains available, and the same error is not assessed again in a later part (sg-23:6, sg-23:8).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for both quantities on a path that returns to its starting point.
errors.name: Magnitude of the displacement reported as the distance travelled
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The response integrates the velocity components, then takes the magnitude, and calls the result the distance travelled.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost because the integrand is not the speed (sg-24:6).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask at which parameter values the curve returns to a point it has already visited.
errors.name: Integration over an interval that traces the curve more than once
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: A length or an area is computed over an angle or parameter interval that covers the same piece of curve twice.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reported value is a multiple of the correct one and the answer point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which of the two numbers is the rate in the horizontal direction.
errors.name: Vector components presented without labels or in the wrong order
errors.observed_behavior: Two correct numbers appear with no indication of which is the horizontal and which the vertical component.
errors.scoring_consequence: The guideline accepts separate components only when they are labelled, so an unlabelled pair can lose a point (sg-23:6).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to check the equality by substituting the value of the parameter.
errors.name: Variable expression equated to a numerical value
errors.observed_behavior: A chain such as an expression in t set equal to its value at one time is written as a single equality.
errors.scoring_consequence: In 2023 such a response earned one of the two available points (sg-23:6); in 2025 an unclear linkage between a correct integral and a correct value was treated as scratch work and cost nothing (sg-25:8).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask how many conditions the initial position supplies.
errors.name: One constant of integration used for both components
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: A vector antiderivative carries a single constant rather than one in each component.
errors.scoring_consequence: The particular solution cannot satisfy both initial conditions, so the answer is wrong.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the same coordinate with a different starting position.
errors.name: Initial position not added to the accumulated change
errors.observed_behavior: The definite integral of a velocity component is reported as the coordinate.
errors.scoring_consequence: The initial condition point is lost and the answer point falls with it (sg-24:7).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which of the two times the position is known at.
errors.name: Accumulation run in the wrong direction in time
errors.observed_behavior: The integral between the known time and the requested time is added when it should be subtracted, or its limits are in the wrong order.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost; the guideline lists several correct arrangements of the subtraction and the limits (sg-24:7).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the equation that the solver was given.
errors.name: Time reported with no speed equation
errors.observed_behavior: A time at which the speed takes a value is given with no equation and no speed expression.
errors.scoring_consequence: Neither the setup point nor the answer point is earned; the words speed equals the value alone also fail to earn the setup point (sg-23:6).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the sine of one and compare with the value the response used.
errors.name: Calculator work performed in degree mode
non_conceptual_causes: calculator left in the wrong mode
errors.observed_behavior: Trigonometric values throughout a question are computed in degree measure, producing internally consistent but wrong numbers.
errors.scoring_consequence: The response does not earn the first point it would otherwise have earned and is generally eligible for the rest (sg-23:6, sg-23:7).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to recompute the speed at one time directly from the components.
errors.name: Incorrect speed expression carried into the distance integral
errors.observed_behavior: The integrand for total distance is an incorrect speed declared in an earlier part.
errors.scoring_consequence: The integral point is earned and the answer point is not (sg-23:8).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the sign of the rate is at a time when the coordinate is positive and decreasing.
errors.name: Direction of motion read from the sign of the coordinate
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The response says the particle approaches an axis on the interval where the coordinate itself is negative.
errors.scoring_consequence: The point for considering the sign of the rate is lost (sg-24:8).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask why the particle is approaching the axis on that interval and not on the rest.
errors.name: Interval reported with no reason
errors.observed_behavior: A correct subinterval of times is given with no statement about the sign of the relevant rate.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer with reason point is lost (sg-24:8).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for both Cartesian coordinates of the point at a stated angle.
errors.name: Polar radius used as a Cartesian coordinate
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The value of r is treated as the x coordinate or the y coordinate of the point.
errors.scoring_consequence: The coordinate is wrong, so any extremum or conversion built on it fails.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the derivative expression before the value.
errors.name: Polar derivative value given with no sign of differentiation
errors.observed_behavior: A correct decimal for dr/dtheta appears with nothing showing that r was differentiated.
errors.scoring_consequence: The point is not earned, because the guideline requires the response to indicate differentiation of r (sg-25:7).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what quantity r measures before the derivative is interpreted.
errors.name: Rate of change of r described as the speed of the particle
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The interpretation of dr/dtheta names the speed along the curve rather than the rate at which the distance from the origin changes.
errors.scoring_consequence: The interpretation is wrong, and the chain rule part built on it reports the wrong quantity.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the units of the requested rate are.
errors.name: Rate of the angle omitted from a chain rule product
errors.observed_behavior: The rate at which the distance from the origin changes with time is reported as dr/dtheta alone.
errors.scoring_consequence: The chain rule point is lost (sg-25:10).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the slope of the tangent to a circle of constant radius, where dr/dtheta is zero.
errors.name: Slope of a polar curve given as dr/dtheta
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports the derivative of r where the slope of the tangent line in the plane was requested.
errors.scoring_consequence: The slope point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to name the two factors in the coordinate before differentiating.
errors.name: Product rule omitted when differentiating r times a trigonometric factor
errors.observed_behavior: The derivative of a Cartesian coordinate in polar form is taken as the product of the two derivatives or of one derivative alone.
errors.scoring_consequence: The derivative and everything built from it are wrong.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the coordinate at each endpoint has been compared with the value at the candidate.
errors.name: Local argument offered for a farthest point
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: A first or second derivative test is presented as the justification that a point on the curve is farthest from an axis.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost while the answer point remains available (sg-25:9).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the equation that the solver was given.
errors.name: Critical angle presented with no equation
errors.observed_behavior: The angle solving the derivative equation is written down with nothing showing what was set equal to zero.
errors.scoring_consequence: The point for considering the derivative equal to zero is not earned (sg-25:9).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the area of a circular sector of stated radius and angle.
errors.name: Factor of one half omitted from a polar area integral
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The area integrand is the square of r with no factor of one half.
errors.scoring_consequence: The value is twice the area, so the answer point is lost; the factor is assessed with the limits (sg-25:7).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the area of a full circle from the polar formula and compare.
errors.name: Polar area integrand written without squaring r
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The integral is of r with respect to theta rather than of the square of r.
errors.scoring_consequence: The first point, which requires an integral containing the square of r, is lost (sg-25:7).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask at which angles the two curves meet.
errors.name: Polar limits taken from the wrong angles
errors.observed_behavior: The area integral runs over the angle interval of the figure rather than between the intersection angles of the two curves.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost, since the limits are assessed there (sg-25:7).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask how many solutions the equation has on the stated interval.
errors.name: One intersection angle not found
errors.observed_behavior: Only one solution of the equation setting the radii equal is found, so the region is bounded incorrectly.
errors.scoring_consequence: The limits are wrong and the answer point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which curve is farther from the origin at an angle inside the interval.
errors.name: Inner and outer polar radii exchanged
errors.observed_behavior: The integrand subtracts the square of the outer radius from the square of the inner radius.
errors.scoring_consequence: A negative area is produced and the integrand point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to evaluate both expressions with the radii two and one.
errors.name: Square of the difference of the radii used in a polar area
non_conceptual_causes: a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The integrand is the square of the difference of the two radius functions rather than the difference of their squares.
errors.scoring_consequence: The integrand point is lost (sg-25:7).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which part of the region the integral just written covers.
errors.name: Symmetry used without the compensating factor
errors.observed_behavior: Half of a symmetric region is integrated and the result is reported without doubling, or a full region is doubled as well.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reported area is half or twice the correct value and the answer point is lost; the correctly doubled form earned all points in 2025 (sg-25:8).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask where the constant of proportionality went.
errors.name: Proportionality written without a constant
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the derivative equal to the quantity itself, with no constant of proportionality.
errors.scoring_consequence: The model is wrong by a factor and every later value built on it is wrong.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the quantity should rise or fall when it starts below the fixed level.
errors.name: Difference reversed in a rate proportional to a gap
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the difference the other way round, so the modelled quantity moves away from the fixed level instead of toward it.
errors.scoring_consequence: The sign of the solution's approach is wrong, and the slope field and the particular solution both follow it.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what each letter stands for and in what units.
errors.name: Variables used with no units or meanings
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The equation is written in letters that are never given meanings or units.
errors.scoring_consequence: An interpretation point that requires the quantity and its units is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which sentence of the problem would change if the starting value were different.
errors.name: Initial condition folded into the differential equation
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the stated value as part of the equation rather than as a separate condition.
errors.scoring_consequence: The equation is not the model asked for and the constant of integration has nothing to be fixed by.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the left side of the written equation measures.
errors.name: Equation written for the quantity rather than its rate
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response produces a formula for the quantity where a differential equation was asked for.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer is of the wrong kind and no separation step can follow.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the left side of the differential equation requires.
errors.name: Candidate substituted without being differentiated
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The verification puts the candidate into both sides and never produces its derivative.
errors.scoring_consequence: The check does not test the equation, so the conclusion is unsupported.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the candidate gives at the stated input.
errors.name: Initial condition not checked before a particular solution is claimed
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response verifies the equation and declares the candidate the particular solution without testing the stated point.
errors.scoring_consequence: A member of the family is reported where a specific one was asked for.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for one input at which the two sides differ.
errors.name: Failure claimed with no disagreeing input exhibited
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response says a candidate is not a solution and shows nothing that fails.
errors.scoring_consequence: The verdict is unsupported even when correct.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to name two different functions that satisfy the same equation.
errors.name: General solution reported as the only solution
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response treats the family with its constant as a single function.
errors.scoring_consequence: The distinction the essential knowledge draws between a family and a particular solution is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the coordinates of the point the slope was computed at.
errors.name: Slope evaluated at the wrong lattice point
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response computes the segment slope using coordinates taken from a neighbouring point of the grid.
errors.scoring_consequence: The drawn or matched field is wrong at the points that distinguish the candidates.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the numerical slope at two points and compare the two segments.
errors.name: Segments drawn with a uniform tilt
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The drawn field uses the same steepness everywhere regardless of the computed slopes.
errors.scoring_consequence: The field carries no information and no solution curve can be read from it.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which values of the quantity make the rate zero.
errors.name: Zero slope locus not identified
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response never solves the right side equal to zero, so the horizontal segments are missed.
errors.scoring_consequence: The equilibrium level is unavailable, which costs the sketch point and the critical point work that follows.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which variables appear in the right side of each candidate.
errors.name: Dependence on a variable misread from the field
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response claims the slope varies along a line on which the printed segments are identical, or the reverse.
errors.scoring_consequence: The match to a candidate equation is made on a false feature.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the drawn curve is tangent to the segment at each point it passes.
errors.name: Solution curve drawn without following the segments
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The drawn curve passes through the point but conflicts with the nearby segments or stops short of the edges of the rectangle.
errors.scoring_consequence: The single sketch point is lost; the guideline lists all four conditions as required.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the rate of change is exactly at that level.
errors.name: Solution curve drawn across an equilibrium level
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The curve rises through the row of horizontal segments that marks the level at which the rate vanishes.
errors.scoring_consequence: The sketch point is lost; the guideline requires the curve to lie entirely on one side of that level.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the slope at a point where the candidates disagree.
errors.name: Field matched on visual impression
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response picks a candidate equation from the general look of the field rather than from computed slopes or the zero slope locus.
errors.scoring_consequence: The match is unsupported and often wrong when two candidates share a feature.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which feature of the field or the equation makes the claim true.
errors.name: Long-run behaviour asserted with no reference to the field or the equation
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response states where solutions are heading without citing the segments or the sign of the right side.
errors.scoring_consequence: A reason point is lost even when the claim is right.

errors.discriminating_probe: Give an increasing concave down solution and ask for the direction of a tangent line estimate.
errors.name: Direction of an approximation claimed from increase or decrease
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response argues that the estimate is high or low because the solution is increasing or decreasing.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reason point is lost; the guideline requires the second derivative, the monotonicity of the first derivative, or the concavity.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask how long each of the stated number of equal steps is.
errors.name: Step size taken as the whole interval
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response uses the full distance to the target input as one step although several equal steps were asked for.
errors.scoring_consequence: The demonstration point is lost because the step size is wrong.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which point the slope is evaluated at on the first step.
errors.name: First Euler step taken with the wrong initial values
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The first step starts from a point other than the given initial condition, or evaluates the derivative at the target input.
errors.scoring_consequence: The demonstration point is lost; the 2025 guideline names the correct initial condition as one of its three conditions.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the input and the output used at the start of the second step.
errors.name: Second Euler step restarted from the initial value
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response evaluates the derivative again at the initial point instead of at the approximation the first step produced.
errors.scoring_consequence: The demonstration point is lost in the 2024 shape, where two correct steps are required.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to label the columns of their own table.
errors.name: Approximation reported with no visible steps
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: A single number appears with no expressions and no labelled table.
errors.scoring_consequence: The demonstration point is lost, and an unlabelled table with a wrong answer earns nothing.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the second derivative does over the interval.
errors.name: Euler direction claimed with no concavity statement
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response says the approximation is an overestimate or an underestimate and never mentions the second derivative or the concavity.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reason point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which terms belong on which side before any integral is written.
errors.name: Variables not separated before antidifferentiating
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response antidifferentiates the equation as written, with both variables on the same side.
errors.scoring_consequence: All four points of the separation part are lost; the guideline states that a response with no separation earns none of them.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what happened to the differential on the other side.
errors.name: Only one side antidifferentiated
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response integrates the dependent side and leaves the independent side untouched, or the reverse.
errors.scoring_consequence: The antiderivative point is lost and every later point with it.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the answer would be if the starting value were different.
errors.name: Constant of integration omitted
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
habit carried over from definite integrals
errors.observed_behavior: The antiderivative equation is written with no constant.
errors.scoring_consequence: At most the first two points are available; the guideline caps the response there.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the value of the dependent variable at a stated input.
errors.name: Answer left implicit when an expression was asked for
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response stops at an equation relating the two variables rather than solving for the dependent one.
errors.scoring_consequence: The final solving point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the right side as a product of two single variable factors.
errors.name: Separation attempted on an equation that does not factor
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response moves terms across as though the right side factored when it is a sum in both variables.
errors.scoring_consequence: The separated form is not equivalent to the equation, so nothing that follows is valid.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which equation the initial values were substituted into.
errors.name: Constant evaluated after the exponentiation instead of before
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response exponentiates first and then substitutes the initial condition into an expression where the constant has changed form.
errors.scoring_consequence: The constant point is at risk; the guideline earns it for including the constant in an equation and substituting the initial values into it.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the enclosed expression is positive or negative at the initial point.
errors.name: Absolute value dropped without checking the sign
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response removes an absolute value from a logarithm without using the initial condition or a stated bound to decide the sign.
errors.scoring_consequence: The branch may contradict the initial condition, which costs the final solving point.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what happens to the formula at the input where its denominator vanishes.
errors.name: Domain restriction omitted or wrongly chosen
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response claims the solution formula holds for every input, or reports an interval that does not contain the initial input.
errors.scoring_consequence: A demanded domain statement is lost and the reported solution overreaches.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the expression gives at the initial input.
errors.name: Accumulation form written without the initial value or the differential
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the particular solution as an integral alone, or omits the differential from it.
errors.scoring_consequence: The expression does not satisfy the initial condition, and a missing differential is a notation loss the Chief Reader records name.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the answer should still contain a constant.
errors.name: General and particular solutions interchanged
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports a formula with an undetermined constant where a particular solution was asked for, or fixes the constant where the general solution was asked for.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer is of the wrong kind for the question posed.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what happens to the rate when the amount doubles.
errors.name: Exponential model written as a linear one
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the quantity as the initial value plus a constant multiple of the independent variable.
errors.scoring_consequence: The model is the wrong family and no later value is right.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the formula gives at the initial input.
errors.name: Exponential solution written with the constant in the wrong place
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the initial value inside the exponent, or the rate constant as a multiplier outside it.
errors.scoring_consequence: The formula fails the initial condition or the differential equation.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which two pieces of data the constant needs.
errors.name: Rate constant read from a single data pair
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response computes the constant from the initial condition alone, with no second value.
errors.scoring_consequence: The constant is undetermined and the reported value is arbitrary.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the number measures and whether the quantity is rising or falling.
errors.name: Interpretation of the rate constant omits units or direction
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports the numerical constant and does not say whether the quantity grows or decays, or in what units.
errors.scoring_consequence: An interpretation point that requires the quantity, the units, and the direction is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which quantity the differential equation constrains.
errors.name: Motion model treated as though the derivative were the position
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response integrates or differentiates in the wrong direction when the modelled quantity is a position or a velocity.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reported quantity is one derivative away from the one asked for.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what happens to the rate when the quantity reaches the carrying capacity.
errors.name: Logistic equation written without the limiting factor
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes a constant multiple of the quantity alone, losing the factor that encodes the carrying capacity.
errors.scoring_consequence: The model is exponential rather than logistic and has no ceiling.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which nonzero value of the quantity makes the rate zero.
errors.name: Carrying capacity read from the wrong factor
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports the constant of proportionality, or zero, as the carrying capacity.
errors.scoring_consequence: Every later value built on the capacity is wrong.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which values of the quantity make the rate positive and which make it negative.
errors.name: Limiting value asserted with no reference to the sign of the rate
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response names a limit without saying why solutions move toward it from the given initial value.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reason point is lost even when the value is right.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the rate exactly at the carrying capacity.
errors.name: Fastest change value reported as the carrying capacity
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response says the quantity changes fastest when it reaches its ceiling.
errors.scoring_consequence: The value is wrong, and it contradicts the equation the response itself wrote.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what each number measures and in what units.
errors.name: Logistic interpretation omits the units or the modelled quantity
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response gives the two numbers and never says what they mean for the population being modelled.
errors.scoring_consequence: An interpretation point is lost because the sentence is incomplete.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which value of the quantity makes the rate zero, before any solving.
errors.name: Logistic equation solved where reasoning from it was asked for
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the question or the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The response separates the logistic equation with partial fractions and solves it in order to report a limit the equation gives directly.
errors.scoring_consequence: Time is spent on work the question did not ask for, and an error inside it costs the value that the equation alone would have given.
